name: Browser Use CLI
description: Operate the configured signed-in browser through the upstream Browser Use CLI and its persistent Browser Harness session.
progressive_guidance:
Prefer inspect/act for individual steps and run for predictable batches. Reuse observed targets. Helpers activate the working tab and record outcomes for shared recovery. A changed page does not establish task completion; inspect failure evidence before retrying or switching tools.

run(code) executes Python with the helpers below pre-imported. Browser state persists across calls; Python variables do not. Keep batches below 60 seconds and print compact JSON for each verified item. The working directory is the session artifact directory. Use screenshot to attach visual evidence.

Tab helpers: list_tabs(), current_tab(), switch_tab(target), new_tab(url), goto_url(url), close_tab(target). Obtain target IDs from observed targetId fields.
Workflow helpers use the same target descriptors as act:
- leon_observe(offset=0, limit=40): optional selector selects returned elements; exposes targets, state_id, total and next_offset. Page through results as needed.
- leon_click(target, expect=None, timeout=10): clicks once, then returns new_tabs, changed-page evidence, or verified form-control focus. Focus alone does not prove a dropdown opened or a value changed. expect can be a read-only JS expression or Python predicate. Inspect a newly opened tab before looking for its download control.
- leon_fill(target, value): verifies the entered value; submission needs a separate action.
- leon_select(target, value): selects one enabled HTML select option using trusted browser keys and verifies its value/index. Use an exact option value from inspect (options are bounded; inspect the control with js for further options). Do not fill a select. For custom ARIA combobox/listbox widgets, click, inspect their visible options, then click the desired option and verify the result. Keep HTML dropdowns in Browser Use, not Cua.
- leon_download(target, expected_text=None, timeout=20): waits for a native download, returns its path, SHA256, size, PDF text and page count. expected_text is a list of document identifiers observed on its page. identity_verified is false when omitted.
- leon_wait(condition, timeout=10): polls a read-only JS expression or Python predicate without repeating input.
Other helpers: page_info(), drain_events(), upload_file(selector, path), js(expression), cdp(method, **params), press_key(key), scroll(x, y, dy=-300, dx=0), wait_for_element(selector, timeout=10, visible=False), wait_for_load(timeout=15). Use visible=True when waiting for visible controls; DOM presence alone is insufficient. Inspect iframe/shadow content explicitly. Verify lower-level action outcomes and avoid synthetic DOM clicks.

Uploads: use upload_file with an observed file-input selector and an authorized absolute file path (or list of paths); it uses CDP without opening the OS picker. File inputs may be hidden: inspect their DOM explicitly with js, including accept/multiple and the associated label. Verify the selected file names/count and the page attachment state afterward; selection alone does not prove upload completion. Do not submit unless authorized. Use leon_download for normal downloads rather than a Save dialog.

Browser JavaScript dialogs: inspect returns ready=false with dialog evidence when page JS is blocked. page_info() also surfaces buffered dialogs; the upstream cache is browser-wide, so confirm the intended tab/message using observed dialog events before responding. Use run with cdp("Page.handleJavaScriptDialog", accept=True or False, promptText="...") for alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload, choosing only what the task authorizes. Do not stub dialogs, auto-accept confirmations, or repeat the triggering input. Reinspect afterward. These are not browser-access or OS permission prompts: for those, pause and ask the owner; never use mac-approve or another automated approval route. Use Cua only for native controls that the browser helpers cannot handle, then return here.

After failure, not_sent means no input was delivered; unverifiable means it may have taken effect. Reinspect instead of replaying blindly. Use the configured browser and installed CLI; leave dependency installation and daemon management to Leon.

run.description: Execute a bounded Python script through Browser Use CLI. Helpers are pre-imported and the browser session persists across calls. Print relevant observations and verified outcomes.

code.description: Python code using the pre-imported helpers listed in progressive guidance. Print compact JSON observations and verified outcomes; do not wrap in shell syntax.

screenshot.description: Capture the current browser tab through the CLI and attach its screenshot to the model. Use run to switch to an observed tab first.

inspect.description: Inspect a tab and return compact visible controls with reusable target descriptors, or ready=false with a pending browser dialog without evaluating blocked page JavaScript. Prefer this to writing inspection scripts.

selector.description: CSS selector for elements to return, such as table button or tbody tr. This is not a container scope. Defaults to controls and rows.

act.description: Use an observed target to click, fill, select an HTML dropdown option, or download. Handles readiness and trusted input; returns verified changes or structured failure evidence without replaying input. Form-control clicks verify focus, not selection or submission.

context.description: Observed row or list-item context; preserves identity when repeated controls share a label.

value.description: For fill: entered text. For select: exact enabled option value observed in inspect.

expect.description: Optional read-only JS postcondition for click; omit to observe page changes/new tabs automatically.

expected_text.description: Only for download. Document identity such as an invoice number observed on its page; do not substitute ledger dates or amounts.
